assertions.name: signal_robust_to_q_symmetrizer
assertions.source: |plain − q-bosonic| signal spread < 0.1 — q₀≈1 makes the symmetrizer choice a sub-10%% effect; the positive, sub-dominant verdict does not depend on plain-vs-q-weighted.

description: q-weighted Young symmetrizer for the ⁴He block-swap binding signal. The Hecke q-symmetrizer E_±=(β±…)/(q+q⁻¹) is a reweighting of the four block-swap traces (no recompute; the (q+q⁻¹)² norm cancels in the signal ratio). Because q₀≈1.11≈1 the q-bosonic signal sits within a few %% of the plain ¼Σ value — the +0.27 production signal (symmetrization relieves the under-prediction, sub-dominant O(1 MeV)) is ROBUST to the symmetrizer choice. Caveat: β (two 3-strand blocks) is not a single Hecke generator, so E_± is a first-order q-deformation, not the exact block R-matrix spectral projector; the w∈{q⁻¹,1,q} spread bounds the residual ambiguity.

data.verdict: The q-weighted (E_+) bosonic signal +0.2970 sits within 0.0241 of the plain +0.2729 — because q₀≈1.11≈1 the symmetrizer choice shifts the signal by only ~9%. The conclusion is ROBUST: POSITIVE (symmetrization relieves the under-prediction), O(1 MeV), sub-dominant. The fermionic (Pauli) projector gives -0.3820 — a distinct sector, not the bosonic ground state.
